media_work.title: The Trial of the Chicago 7
media_work.focus_or_theme: Political prosecution, judicial bias, anti-Vietnam War protests, civil rights, free speech.
media_work.summaryNotes: Depicts the controversial trial related to the 1968 Democratic National Convention protests.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Political prosecution, judicial bias, anti-Vietnam War protests, civil rights, free speech.
media_item.summary_notes: Aaron Sorkin's film dramatizes the tumultuous trial of activists following the 1968 DNC protests. It highlights issues of government overreach, judicial prejudice (particularly from Judge Hoffman), and the clash between counterculture movements and the establishment during the Vietnam War era. While convictions occurred, they were largely seen as politically motivated and were mostly overturned on appeal, making it distinct from cases where factual innocence is the primary issue.
systemic_issues_raw: Clash between counterculture movements and the establishment during the Vietnam War era

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: One of the Chicago 7, charged with conspiracy and inciting riots at the 1968 DNC protests. Convicted on some charges after a biased trial, but the convictions were later overturned on appeal. The case is considered a matter of unjust prosecution rather than a standard wrongful conviction.
